- Keep “Always” only for true background needs (e.g., real turn‑by‑turn with screen off, fitness tracking, geofenced automations). Everything else: downgrade to “While Using” or “Never.”

- Limit background access to a very small set of trusted apps that directly power commute/nearby features. Prefer geofencing over constant tracking when available.

- Android: App info > Battery > Restricted for apps that don’t need to run in the background. (Background data is separate; most people only need the battery restriction.)

- iPhone: Settings > Privacy & Security → Apple Advertising (turn off) and “Allow Apps to Request to Track” (restrict tracking).
- Android: Turn off ad personalization in Google settings.

- Review access to Microphone, Camera, Photos, Contacts, Bluetooth; set to Ask/While Using unless full‑time access is essential.

7) Use your privacy dashboard
- Check the system privacy dashboard periodically to see recent access to location/mic/camera; if something surprises you, revoke or reduce it.

8) Spot background abuse quickly
- Watch battery usage for unexpected hogs and the location icon appearing when you’re not using an app; remove “Always” or turn off background access for offenders.

9) iPhone system services
- Settings > Privacy & Security > Location Services > System Services → turn off Significant Locations; keep essentials like Emergency Calls & SOS, Find My iPhone, and similar core items.

10) Re‑audit periodically
- Revisit permissions for older apps and anything newly installed; keep precise/background access limited to the smallest necessary set.

This setup preserves normal use (maps, rideshare, weather, commute updates) while minimizing constant, detailed tracking.
